newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was at a standstill on Monday, with packer buyers and cattle owners $3.00 per cwt apart in bids and asking levels, feedlot sources said.
Inquiry was light, with packer bids $62.00 to $63.00 passed by owners pricing cattle $65.00 to mostly $66.00.
Many feedlots reportedly remained extremely current following last week's heavy volume, they said.
Prices this week were expected steady to $1.00 higher than last week's top of $64.00 on ideas packers were short-bought and picked up many of the cattle at midweek last week.
Outlooks for higher fed cattle prices were diluted by last Friday's bearishly-construed USDA monthly cattle on feed report.

The USDA report showed January feedlot placements 25 percent greater than a year ago, which greatly exceeded trade estimates. CME live cattle futures were called to open 0.50 cent per lb lower in April on Tuesday and 1.00 cent lower in June and August.
Several beef slaughtering plants were closed on Monday in observance of the U.S. Presidents' Day holiday.
